**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply list margins only at list boundaries**

For consecutive list items, assigning `list_margin` to `pending_margin` adds that margin between every pair of items, even when the `li` style has zero margins. With the profile in `test_layout_sizing.py`, a three-item list is estimated at 154 px rather than 126 px (32 px padding, 66 px of text, and two 14 px outer list margins). This excess grows with every item and causes ordinary lists to receive unnecessarily tall components. Preserve the item's bottom margin between adjacent items and apply the list margin when entering or leaving the list.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Leave Markdown images unestimated like HTML images**

When content contains a standard Markdown image such as `![plot](https://example.com/plot.png)`, this expression replaces the image with its alt text. The HTML-only guard in `estimate_markdown()` does not detect it, so the estimator reports a confident text-height range even though the image's rendered height is unknown. With the supplied test profile, that example recommends only nine grid units, which can severely clip a normal chart image. Detect Markdown images and return the same unestimated result used for unsupported HTML rather than measuring their alt text.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

payload.follow_up: Detectar imagens Markdown antes da medição textual e acrescentar teste de regressão para o resultado não estimado.
payload.headline: Imagens Markdown recebem uma estimativa textual indevida
payload.before: A imagem é reduzida ao texto alternativo e recebe uma faixa restrita sem ressalva, embora sua altura seja desconhecida.
payload.after: Imagens Markdown recebem o resultado não estimado usado para HTML: approximate=true, motivo explícito e faixa completa da grade.
payload.motivation: Evitar que consumidores dimensionem componentes com base em uma altura textual que não representa a imagem renderizada.
payload.reply: Confirmed with the test profile: the Markdown image returns (8, 9, 20), approximate=false and no reasons, exactly like its alt text. The equivalent HTML image is correctly marked unestimated. Markdown images need the same fallback and a regression test.
